title: Service stability transformation: sprint patterns, risk scenarios, and stakeholder cadence
content:
Purpose:
This is a working plan for a cross-functional push to shrink incident surface and improve SLO adherence by Q4 2026. The doc focuses on a repeatable sprint pattern, realistic risk scenarios to rehearse, stakeholder cadence, and lightweight success metrics so engineering, product, and SRE teams can coordinate quickly.

Context and problem statement:
- We have growing traffic and more model variants. Operational surprises remain the primary source of user-visible latency spikes and error-rate regressions.
- SLO coverage exists for top-level API routes but many product teams lack clear remediation playbooks and ownership for SLI drift.
- Goal: build a small, repeatable cross-functional sprint pattern that reduces time-to-detect and time-to-fix for SLO breaches and institutionalizes handoff/ownership.

High-level approach (what good looks like):
- Monthly focused 2-week "stability sprint" per product domain (hosted-api, dedicated, private) with clear KPI targets and a post-sprint retro.
- Each sprint includes: a scenario rehearsal (tabletop), an SLI audit & small remediation backlog, and one instrumentation change (alert/trace/dash).
- Decision rule: if a service's P99 latency or error-rate crosses SLO threshold for 3 non-consecutive days in a 14-day window, it becomes a sprint candidate.

Sprint pattern (2-week template):
Week 0: Pre-sprint (planning, data pull, invite stakeholders)
- Owner: product lead + product reliability rep
- Deliverables: top-5 SLI time-series, heatmap of error sources, proposed scenario to rehearse
- Tools: dashboard snapshot, linked ticket board, scenario script

Week 1: Deep-dive & remediation execution
- Day 1: Kickoff (30–60m) with eng, SRE, product, infra, and support reps. Review top issues and risks.
- Day 2–4: Triage and small remediation tickets (<=3 engineering days each). Prioritize changes that improve signal, observability, or cheap mitigations (timeouts, circuit-breaker tuning).
- Day 5: Mid-sprint checkpoint; update dashboard and call out blockers.

Week 2: Scenario rehearsal & closure
- Day 6–8: Run tabletop or canary-failure scenario in a staging-like environment (simulate increased load, partial model fallback, degraded KV cache). Capture runbook gaps.
- Day 9: Implement prioritized low-effort fixes from rehearsal findings (alert tuning, postmortem templates, runbook snippets).
- Day 10: Sprint review & retro. Produce 3 concrete follow-ups and owners.

Roles & responsibilities (lightweight):
- Sprint Lead: product reliability rep (schedules, drives decisions).
- SRE Lead: runs the tabletop, verifies alerting and observability changes, ensures rollback procedures are documented.
- Service Owner: engineers responsible for the code path; owns remediation PRs and validation.
- Incident Liaison (on-call engineer): validates runbook steps and time-to-detect improvements.
- Support/CS rep: provides customer-impact evidence and priority signals.

Risk scenarios to rehearse (examples to rotate across sprints):
- Model variant fallback: primary model fails (OOM/timeout) and automatic fallback to smaller variant causes quality drop and unknown edge errors. Test fallback gating, perf, and telemetry.
- KV cache degradation: sustained 30–50% increase in cache misses leading to backend stalls and increased p99. Validate circuit breakers and backpressure.
- Tokenization/encoding regressions: malformed input causes a line of code to throw and cascade to request failures. Validate input sanitization and business-logic guards.
- Network partition between routing layer and GPU pool: some requests queue; check autoscaling/fallback and customer-visible tail latency.
- Dependency/API quota exhaustion: third-party embedding service hits quota, causing internal retries and burst failures. Validate bulkhead patterns and degraded-mode behaviors.

Observability & instrumentation changes (minimal set per sprint):
- Add or refine one SLI per sprint (e.g., service-level end-to-end success %, model-fallback rate, prefix-cache hit rate).
- Create a short-run dashboard panel + one alert with clear thresholds and runbook link.
- Add a trace-sampling rule targeted to high-error traces for debugging.

Success metrics (short-term):
- Mean time to acknowledge SLO violation (MTTAcknowledge) <= 15 minutes for covered services within sprint cohort.
- Number of identical SLO-regressions month-over-month reduced by 30% in selected cohort after 3 sprints.
- At least one reduced-cost mitigation (e.g., caching change or batching) implemented per sprint that reduces per-token compute or P95 latency.

Cross-functional handoffs & escalation flow:
- If a remediation needs >3 engineering days, escalate to product + eng leadership for prioritization (use JIRA key with "slo-blocker" label).
- Post-sprint: capture follow-ups in a shared board; SRE to own long-lived monitoring work, product to own behavioral change or product-level rollouts.

Lightweight runbook template (to keep in sprint ticket):
- Problem statement (one sentence)
- Trigger condition (SLI threshold)
- Steps to identify root cause (dashboard links, queries)
- Short-term mitigation (how to reduce user impact)
- Owner for remediation PR and owner for monitoring/validation
- Postmortem owner and timeline (if incident)

Communication cadence & stakeholders:
- Kickoff (Day 1): core team (engineering, SRE, product reliability, infra), 30–60m
- Mid-sprint pulse (Day 5): 15m async notes + two attendees in quick sync
- Scenario rehearsal readout (Day 8): 30m, share recording + action board
- Sprint retro (Day 10): 60m, capture 3 follow-ups and assign owners
- Monthly exec summary: 1–2 slide highlight reel (SRE lead) for Eng leadership and Product heads

Open questions / gotchas to decide before pilot (needed from leadership):
- How many concurrent sprints can SRE reasonably support? (scoping: 2–3 per month vs. 5+)
- Budget/priority for dedicated staging capacity to run realistic canary failures (who funds?)
- Which SLOs are "must-cover" vs. "nice-to-have" for this program? Need a simple triage rubric.

Immediate next steps (this doc is the kickoff artifact):
1) Align on pilot cohort: pick 3 candidate services (hosted text gen, embeddings API, model-router) — owner: Maya Chen — due 2026-02-22
2) Schedule pilot sprint calendar for March 2026 (2-week window) — owner: Amina Patel — due 2026-02-25
3) Create shared sprint board & seed with the SLI snapshots and one rehearsal script per service — owner: Diego Rivera — due 2026-02-26
4) Confirm staging capacity with infra & private deployments team for one rehearsal run — owner: Liam O'Connor — due 2026-02-28

Notes to self / informal reminders:
- Keep remediation tickets small and mergeable within a sprint; defer larger architecture changes to backlog planning.
- Watch for alert fatigue: prefer fewer, higher-signal alerts and leverage runbook links.
- Use the pull request template to include "slo-impact" checklist for reviewers.

Attachments / artifacts to create during pilot:
- Short rehearsal script (markdown) per service (put in Confluence page CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM-9876)
- Sprint board: JIRA project RPO with label slo-sprint-2026-march
- One-slide template for exec summary (keeps the ask minimal)

End — comments welcome. This is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight; the intent is to make the reliability program feel like a series of small, targeted sprints rather than a monolithic org-wide program.
